Kearns, D., Liu, H. and Consoli, C. (2021). Technology Readiness and Costs of CCS. Global CCS Institute, March 2021. Circular Carbon Economy: Keystone to Global Sustainability series. https://www.globalccsinstitute.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/CCE-CCS-Technology-Readiness-and-Costs-22-1.pdf

Page numbers are printed page numbers, which equal PDF page numbers (cover = p.1). Loaded: TRL 2020 (2014 in notes) for 25 capture technologies from Table 2 (pp.11-12) and for CO2 transport and storage options (Sects. 5-6); Allam cycle capture rate; GCCSI MEA model assumptions (Table A1: 8% discount, 30 yr, 90% CF, 90% capture, 3-yr build) and max single-train capacities (0.6 Mtpa NGCC, 1.4 Mtpa SCPC); printed levelized costs: assumed USD2020 0-10/t conditioning for NG processing, fertiliser, bioethanol and ethylene oxide (Fig. 12 note 4), >USD180/t at 1 kPa (aluminium smelter), Ion water-lean 39-44, Saipem enzyme 28 (free waste heat) with 2.4 GJ/t hot water, Boundary Dam 105, Petra Nova 70, study averages 95 (c.2010) and 50 (from 2025); solvent regeneration energy 5.5 / 3.0 / <2.5 GJ/t; storage costs (NPC USD 1-18/t; ZEP 2013 six European scenarios printed as figure labels). NOT in the main file: Figs. 11-17 bar and curve values (no printed labels) - the capture cost by industrial source (cement, steel, refinery, power) exists only as a chart, so read-from-chart approximations are in _other-values; Table 4 partial pressures also in _other-values. Traps: (1) Fig. 12 excludes compression, but Petra Nova / Fig. 16 are capture AND compression, and Boundary Dam says only capture costs. (2) The 0-10 USD/t for concentrated sources is an assumption, not a model result. (3) Table 2 lists Carbon Engineering as the calcium-looping vendor (DAC context). (4) Ion, Saipem, NPC and ZEP figures carry no price year; publication year 2021 used and flagged. (5) USD2020 model costs are escalated from an Aspen 2019 basis (Handy-Whitman).
